title: Linguistic-Typology Diversity Profiles: Are Models a Monoculture Across Languages?

original_idea.body:
# Linguistic-Typology Diversity Profiles

Use typological sampling (balanced languages across families) and measure inter-model homogeneity per language on translated open-ended prompts to test whether low-resource languages show higher homogeneity. Inference + embeddings.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (low-resource-language homogeneity is a structured risk) but the catastrophic link is diffuse.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: typological sampling + per-language homogeneity on translated prompts; translation/sampling adds care.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (per-language homogeneity profile) with translation as a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 5: under-served low-resource-language populations, diffuse long-horizon fairness/systemic risk labs deprioritize, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on multilingual prompts + embeddings, light.

novelty.reasoning: Multilingual homogeneity with typological tools is plausibly open though related work exists.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cross-language homogeneity with typological framing is plausibly open.
